turns.t: Doctor, this is Liam. Back from Thailand on Saturday, fever and a rash. His mam's with him. ~
Thanks, Niamh. Hello Liam, hello Mrs Doyle. What's been happening? ~
Fever. Rash.
He's not a man for words, doctor. Let me say it. He's had the fever since he got back, and the rash came out the day after.
Liam, how long have you had the fever, in your own words?
Three days.
It's not three days, it's a week. I took his temperature at the airport on the Saturday before last and it was up then.
So, you say three days, your mother says closer to a week. I'll put that down as three to seven days, and we'll see if we can narrow it.
Feels like three.
Fair enough. Where's the rash?
Chest, back. Bit on my arms.
It's red spots, not itchy, he says.
Any bleeding, from the gums or nose, or in the stool?
No. None.
Are you allergic to any medicines, any allergies at all?
No.
And are you taking anything at the moment?
Doxycycline, 100 mg once a day, for malaria. I took it all trip. Missed a couple.
He has tablets left, I saw the packet. ~
What were you up to in Thailand? Any insect bites, rural areas, fresh water swimming?
Beaches. Island. Loads of mosquito bites.
Doctor, his obs. ~
Go on, Niamh. ~
Temperature 38.6, pulse 104, blood pressure 118 over 70.
Thank you. Liam, let me look at the rash. ~
Okay.
Fine, flat red spots over the chest and back, and they blanch when I press them.
What does that mean? ~
It means the spots fade under pressure, which is a more reassuring sign. But with a fever and recent tropical travel, I can't take chances. ~
What is it? ~
Most likely a viral illness, such as dengue, picked up from the mosquitoes, but I need the experts to look at you today.
Today? ~
Yes. I'm going to refer you to the infectious diseases team at the hospital and ring them now, they'll see you this afternoon.
I'll write out the letter, doctor. ~
Please. Liam, take paracetamol only if you have to, and don't take ibuprofen or aspirin until they've seen you.
Right. ~
I'll drive him up. ~
Please do, and go straight there. ~

physical_examination.finding: flat red spots over the chest and back

clinical_actions.description: Refer to infectious diseases team for same-day assessment
Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin until seen

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient says the fever has lasted three days; his mother says about a week; summarised by the doctor as three to seven days but not confirmed.

social_history.description: Recent travel to a tropical island with mosquito bites

contradictions_detected: Duration of fever: patient three days vs family member about a week (approximate range only).
